QUTest.alpha_v: joint computational-Z outcome distribution over ALL measured qubits (the test file declares m = measure q).  The declared output register selects which marginals the SUITE asserts, not what the interface observes.  The endpoint state vector is reachable only by the entangled predicate; the transpiled circuit only by gateset and depth
QUTest.A_v: 12 built-in assertion families in a closed 13-member PragmaKind enum
QUTest.Adm_v: 5 behavioural count-substrate families: marginal, observable (Z strings), probability, entropy, distribution
QUTest.U_v: closed and finite per program: |U_v(n)| = 2^(n+1) + n + 1
QUTest.closure_evidence: parser surface == dispatch surface == 12; raise on unrecognised assertion, no fall-through; entry_points declares only console_scripts, no plugin group; no Assertion base class
QUTest.decision_rule: atol tolerance, unanimity over R repetitions
QUTest.external_pair_execution: SUPPORTED (a pair is an OpenQASM 3 test file)

QuCheck.alpha_v: measurement counts on tester-chosen qubits in a tester-chosen X, Y or Z basis; MeasurementConfiguration admits one arbitrary circuit per qubit, so the observation space is continuous
QuCheck.A_v: six assertion constructors: assert_equal, assert_different, assert_probability, assert_entangled, assert_separable, assert_most_frequent
QuCheck.Adm_v: the frozen profile's chosen subset; assert_equal in the arms used here
QuCheck.U_v: OPEN at tool scope; CLOSED once a profile fixes basis, qubits and constructors
QuCheck.closure_evidence: Property and Assertion are abc.ABC with abstract methods; input_generators are user-extensible
QuCheck.decision_rule: Fisher exact per (qubit, basis) with Holm-Bonferroni at family-wise alpha; NOT a theta tolerance
QuCheck.evidence_depth_possible: FULL_CERTIFICATION only under a frozen profile

Muskit.provenance: PyPI sdist Muskit-0.0.3.tar.gz, publisher SHA256 verified; repository github.com/EnautMendi/QuantumMutationQiskit
Muskit.alpha_v: joint computational-Z counts over ALL qubits at a chosen basis-state input, i.e. the SAME observation as QUTest; the interfaces differ in A_v, not alpha_v. executeMutants appends .measure(q[i], c[i]) for every qubit regardless of any declared output register, then runs Aer qasm_simulator at numShots and writes the counts dict to results.txt
Muskit.A_v: EMPTY.  A source-wide search of all 8 modules for assert, expect, oracle, verdict, kill, survive, detect, compare, equal, passed, failed, threshold and tolerance returns nothing.  The tool records outputs; it does not judge them
Muskit.U_v: EMPTY (no assertion language exists to enumerate)
Muskit.closure_evidence: functionalities.py has createMutants, executeMutants, add, replace, remove, getInfo, createInputs only; no comparison logic
Muskit.extension_boundary: not applicable; the user supplies inputs, not oracles
Muskit.decision_rule: NONE.  Muskit produces no kill/survive verdict
Muskit.evidence_depth_possible: RELATION_LEVEL (its counts decide R_O); it cannot support R_A or R_T, so no downstream negative certificate
Muskit.external_pair_execution: SUPPORTED with a representational adapter: getInfo is a line parser requiring QuantumRegister(, QuantumCircuit(, ClassicalRegister( and <circuit>.<gate>(...[q]) lines
Muskit.structural_restriction: Qiskit Python source in that textual shape; our pairs are gate lists, so a generic gate-list -> canonical .py adapter is required

QMutPy.provenance: recovered exactly, not guessed: qmutpy-experiments commit 06cc1b29f7cd443c761d43afec48abea4a1055f6 -> tools/get-tools.sh:156-166 pins github.com/danielfobooss/mutpy branch all_gates at commit 13ab3845b26a18510bf3e0bddd529187f0b86b71; the same script pins qiskit-aqua stable/0.9 at 59d2fa05983e4279ff0ce9e344e9a071e661c7e6 and Python 3.7.0
QMutPy.provenance_confidence: HIGH: the replication artifact pins an exact commit, so no revision had to be inferred from history
QMutPy.alpha_v: NONE OF ITS OWN.  QMutPy is a MutPy fork: it mutates the target module's AST and delegates the verdict to the project's own unittest or pytest suite (mutpy/test_runners/{unittest,pytest}_runner.py).  Whatever the user test observes is the observation
QMutPy.A_v: the host language: ordinary Python unittest/pytest assertions written by the user; QMutPy contributes quantum MUTATION operators (qgates.py QuantumGateDeletion/Insertion/Replacement, qmeasurements.py QuantumMeasurementDeletion/Insertion), not assertions
QMutPy.Adm_v: unbounded; inherited from the user's Python test suite
QMutPy.closure_evidence: controller.py loads a target module and mutates it; the verdict comes from UnittestMutationTestResult / pytest runner
QMutPy.decision_rule: a mutant is killed when the user's test suite fails or errors
QMutPy.evidence_depth_possible: PROFILE_ONLY for this study: the architecture is a quantum mutation engine plus an open Python test suite, so it supplies no bounded assertion surface of its own
QMutPy.external_pair_execution: EXTERNAL_PAIR_EXECUTION_NOT_SUPPORTED: controller.run() drives target_loader.load(...) -> mutate_module(...); there is no facility to accept an externally supplied mutant while preserving the QMutPy interface

pytest.provenance: frozen profile record; BOUNDARY CONTROL, not a peer quantum testing framework
pytest.alpha_v: the endpoint quantum state through the Python program object; any value reachable from it
pytest.A_v: the assert statement over the general Python expression grammar
pytest.closure_evidence: installed distribution declaring an entry point
pytest.evidence_depth_possible: RELATION_LEVEL: constructive witness and state/observation comparison, but no exhaustive negative conclusion
